correctness.rationale: For scalar i.i.d. nonnegative curvature A with mu>0 and finite v, single-step batch mean curvature has mean mu and second moment d=mu^2+v/S. The exact AdaScale population-gain definition from the original algorithm gives r_S=q/d with q=mu^2+v, a constant after cancellation of the common state second-moment factor. Conditioning on x_t, E[(1-alpha r_S Abar)^2]=1+[q/d](alpha^2 q-2alpha mu), independent of x_t. Fresh batches yield E[x_t^2]=Q^t x0^2. Therefore the sharp base-rate MSE contraction interval is 0<alpha<2mu/q independent of S; minimizing Q gives alpha*=mu/q, Q*=v/(S mu^2+v). Plain S-fold linear scaling has the strictly smaller bound 2mu/(S mu^2+v) for S>1. Handles v=0 and zero-iterate continuation.
